title: Read a line graph: extremes and changes between points
subtitle: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots are this one** — 8 Easy, 0 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see a line graph over time, such as years, days, or intervals.
- The question asks which point is highest or lowest, which one has a stated value, or during which interval the change, increase, or decrease was greatest.
- The choices are time labels or intervals, not numbers.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For extremes or a stated value, find that height on the vertical axis and read the matching time.
- 2) For 'greatest change' between intervals of equal width, compare the vertical drop or rise of each segment; the steepest segment wins.
- 3) Check whether the question means increase only, decrease only, or change in either direction.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer an 'increase' question with the biggest decrease, pick the highest point when asked for the lowest, or compare the endpoint values instead of the change across each interval.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You answer an 'increase' question with the biggest decrease, pick the highest point when asked for the lowest, or compare the endpoint values instead of the change across each interval.
